utterances.text: I would like to tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 12103 becomes Exhibit P475, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence. Since I hear from left and right different comments on the number, Madam Registrar, would you carefully verify that it's the right number. Meanwhile you may proceed, Ms. Harbour.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: Today at transcript -- temporary transcript page 36, you were asked about the role of the MUP with respect to the SRK, and you said that occasionally MUP forces were used in specific operations where they might be placed under temporary command. If we could turn to 65 ter 3986, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: This is a 15th of December 1993 order from the SRK commands to the commands of all brigades and others. If you could read the first paragraph to yourself, I would like to understand how this order fits into your prior comments regarding the MUP -- MUP forces.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the example I think I was referring to earlier on relating, I believe, to Operation Lukavac 93. I'd have to see the next page to be sure of that. But this particular operation shows that various units are passed to the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps such as, for example, we see one brigade from the 1st Krajina Corps and one brigade from the Herzegovina Corps, as well as in this case mentioned MUP forces up to a strength of one battalion. And then it says 500 people, 500 personnel. And also mentions VJ special forces up to 120 people and a helicopter squad. So this is an example of the formation of additional units being passed to the corps for their use for a specific operation for a specific purpose. There's no reason to believe that these troops would remain under the command of the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps. At the end of the operation, at the end of the tasks that were carried, then those brigades would be returned to their appropriate corps, and the MUP, as we've heard, returned to its own command structure outside the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: I would like to tender this document, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The witness asked to see the second page. Could it be shown to him.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: There is no second page, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There is no second page. Then we hereby decide that it will not be shown to him.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, before I do that I would just confirm that previous document, as it was told, is 12103 is P475. And the next document 65 ter 3986 becomes Exhibit P476, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P476 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: You discussed with Mr. Lukic the document that is now admitted as Exhibit D94 which were the minutes of a meeting on the 4th of January, 1995, at the SRK command.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: If we could please pull up D94. And I would like to turn to General Milosevic's comments, which start on page 10 in the English, but if we could just go directly to page 11 and to the last page in the B/C/S version.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: General Milosevic states, among other things, in item 6: "As for the training, the order, instruction will soon be issued, which should be implemented." In item 11: "Issue of moral strengthening, we must work on lifting the level of moral," which may be morale, "among the soldiers." Item 12: "Brigade commanders must define what needs to be done to improve the level of combat readiness plan." Number 14: "Reporting must be correct and timely." And you can review the remaining points. What do these comments indicate about this meeting regarding the command and control system?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: At this meeting all the brigade commanders were present, and as I remember from what we saw earlier each of them at a specific time gave a detailed report on the structure and capabilities of each brigade. And from this has come a series of conclusions from the commander, and the commander then gives those directives verbally, and later probably in a requirement form, as a directive to each of the brigade commanders to ensure that the level of training he requires is being met, that the reports that they are writing match the requirements of the logistics organisation so that he can resupply them as required. This is a good example of a commander talking to his troops directly, that is, his commanders of his brigades, directly so that he can establish a -- a good level of training and improve the morale and fighting capability of the soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: If we could turn to Exhibit P338, please, and turn to page 9. Your Honours, I have a quote from this page. I wanted to direct you to it. I can't seem to locate it on the page right now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you slowly read the first three words, then we might be able to find it. If it's on this page.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: "The involvement of different Main Staff bodies in the brigades and other units yielded particularly good results."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I've got paragraph 2.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Paragraph 2, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours, and Mr. Philipps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The word "de" is the last word on that line, seventh line of the second paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: I'll start from the beginning: "The involvement of different Main Staff bodies in the brigades and other units yielded particularly good results because, in that way, directives, commands, and orders reached those who were who execute them in the fastest possible way and the planned concerted action was relatively quickly performed." And there is from an analysis of the combat readiness and the activities of the VRS in 1992. If we look further down the page, it states: "Irrespective --"

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Would the counsel please provide the reference for the original in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: That is something I'm unable to do at the moment, Your Honours. Perhaps the Defence could assist.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I think we need page 9 in B/C/S. Second-last paragraph from the bottom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And I think, in English, it's page 9 as well, of this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Lukic. That -- was that -- that is the reference for the first paragraph. If we could turn to page 10 in the B/C/S for the next reference, which is the very last sentence on page 9 in the English. It is two paragraphs below the bullet points. And I will read: "Irrespective of the aggravating circumstances and factors which adversely affected the morale of fighters and units, we stress that, on the whole, it has been good and stable," and if we could turn the page in English, thank you, "despite the difficulties imposed by the war so that control and command echelons can count on it for the execution of pending missions."

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: Mr. Philipps, what conclusions can you draw from this document regarding the overall functioning of the VRS during this period?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document is a very comprehensive and detailed studies of the capabilities both in terms of fighting and logistics of the VRS. And it shows the attention to detail required for the level of training, preparedness of soldiers. Morale issues, keeping the level of morale high, interestingly enough, in the earlier paragraph we mentioned direct action by the Main Staff within brigade units. And that's an unusual circumstance where it does appear that there has been a -- a change in the chain of command where the VRS Main Staff has directly given orders to a brigade. That's what I -- my implication from the previous paragraph. And that would be a very unusual situation, and I think the reason it's mentioned is because it's an unusual occurrence. But they have found that it's speeded things up. Specifically mentioned. So that's one of the most unusual things that I see from this document. And the rest of it appears to cover the types of problems that you'd expect in any large organisation that requires a high level of training, and they're continually looking for what courses people need to do, what level of training they require.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: Your Honours, on the 30th of October, 2012, the Chamber indicated that where an issue was challenged on cross-examination, the Prosecution might tender the underlying documents of an expert report via a bar table rather than discussing them on re-direct. Several such topics came up during the cross-examination of this witness, which I think could be clarified simply by the documents being available to the Chamber. However, the Chamber specifically asked about -- well, including the -- the Chamber -- the issue of Cedo Sladoje and his position as chief of the operations and training organ. I would be happy to use that vehicle. However, with respect to Cedo Sladoje, since the Chamber specifically asked about it at transcript page 4730, if the Chamber would wish or prefer that I address that with the witness, I could do so. And the same goes for the lengthy discussion on cross-examination of the Vogosca Tactical Group or Operational Group. If it would assist the Chamber, I will use -- discuss these issues with the witness. However, I will leave that in your hands.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Ms. Harbour, since the matter was discussed, and, therefore, there's a chance that it's not merely looking at some documents, but therefore the Chamber would prefer if you would raise that with the witness. I do not know how much time that would take.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: Are you referring to the issue of Cedo Sladoje or to the Vogosca?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Both.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: Both. Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And how much time would that take approximately.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: Perhaps ten more minutes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ten more minutes. Then you have ten more minutes to do that. I already inform the parties that today we will finish at 2.00 and not 2.15 for very practical reasons. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: Turning first to the matter of Cedo Sladoje, if we could please have 65 ter number 12097.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: Yesterday there was quite some discussion between the pages of 4724 and 4730 in the transcript of Cedo Sladoje's position as -- and the existence of the operations and training organ. And here, if we turn -- this -- if we look at this document, which is from 5 November 1993, a regular combat report, from the SRK command to the VRS Main Staff, if we look at page 2 in the English and the first page in B/C/S, the very last paragraph of page 2 -- actually, I will let you read that, and if you could give us any comments, any additional light that you could shed on the issue of Cedo Sladoje and his role.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was a daily combat report from the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps dated, as you say, the 5th November, 1993. And it's one of the documents I used -- documents I used to place Sladoje in the operations and training area of the staff. And we can see that he is named there Colonel Cedo Sladoje as being assistant to the chief of operations and training, PNONO. And also we later see mentioned, for example, Captain First Class Bukva who was the individual who wrote the critique of the politicisation of the corps by the later commander.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: As you said, this is one of the documents underlying your chart.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: And I would tender this into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 12097 becomes Exhibit P477, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: Turning to the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. There may be a little bit of a translation issue with the coma between PNONO and Colonel Cedo Sladoje. There appears a coma whereas in the original it appears there's a full -- there's a dot, apparently, serving to indicate that it's an abbreviation. So these are not in the translation. You could not exclude that one person was mentioned by function and then one person by name. But it seems that in the original it's "puk," and then full spot. Pukovnik, I take it, but abbreviated. Therefore, the coma after PNONO seems to be not accurate. But it could that be -- I'm not a B/C/S speaker, so -- but, Mr. Lukic, if you would agree with that. You see that, Ms. Harbour, that there's a comma --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm trying to see it myself. It's on the bottom of the page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. It says "PNONO puk. Sladoje." Now in the translation a comma is introduced which seems not to be there in the original and which --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Probably they want just in the translation to make it more clear which rank belongs to which --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But if -- in the way it is translated, it is ambiguous as to whether the PNONO is the same person as Colonel Cedo Sladoje. It's ambiguous. I'm not saying ...

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Well, to be honest with you, I don't know what PNONO means.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, that's explained in the translation, the assistant to the chief of operations. I think we have seen that word before. Could we invite the witness, what I just said and looking at the screen, Mr. Philipps --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- any further comment to what I said?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Each individual is referred to, first of all, with his post and then with his rank and then with his name. And then that would mean that the comma is merely a confusion that's been added later. So it's the Chief of Staff, Colonel Milosevic; the assistant to the chief of operations and training, Colonel Sladoje; and then we have the security organ, Captain First Class Bukva. So it seems that there's the -- the post of the individual and then their rank and then their name followed by a comma.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Although it's not consistently done because of -- because of [indiscernible].

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: I believe "puk" - and Mr. Lukic can confirm - "puk" is the abbreviation for "colonel."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. No, I'm just saying that where there appears a dot to explain an abbreviation, which is not used in the translation, there the word is spelled out in its entirety. That's one. And the second is that the comma has been added which may create some confusion but as far as I can see should not be there. Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The problem that on our page in B/C/S I cannot Kosovac at all. Probably --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But that's because there we have to go the -- yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You see for Kosovac no position is explained.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes. There is no position.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But I would like to focus on Sladoje because that was our subject matter. It seems that no one disagrees. Let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: I had tendered the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: Did we already receive a --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, I don't think we did. Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We did. It was assigned number P477.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P477. No loud speaking, mister -- Mr. Mladic. Mr. Mladic, no loud speaking. No. Madam Registrar, the document is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: Let's turn now to the issue of the Vogosca Tactical Group or Operational Group. We discussed this yesterday at transcript page 4742 and again today from temporary transcript pages 5 to 7. And you said yesterday that the Vogosca Tactical Group or Operational Group, that these two groups were likely not the same thing and it may have been disbanded and reformed. If we could now look at some of the documents underlying your index, the first one is 65 ter 12048, which is on your index as Y000-0947. This is a 15 September 1992 order establishing the Vogosca "Operations Group." If we look down at the second paragraph, under item 2, we read: "Preparations have been made for activities along the Bare-Stupska Petlja stretch and partial moving of the line with the aim of improving tactical positions. The Rogarica," which may be Rogatica, "Brigade engaged in active combat. From the units of Ilidza, Ilijas, Igman Rajlovac, and Vogosca brigades, we ... form an operations group. We have appointed Colonel Vukota Vukotic as the commander of the group and his command post will be in the area of Blazuj." If you could please comment on this Mr. Philipps.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is it clearly a report from the corps command up to the Main Staff of the VRS giving details of the formation of this Operational Group. So it's a very clear document putting each of those four brigades, at that particular in time, the intention to form an Operational Group on that date. How long that group lasts and when it's disbanded is not clear, but that's the intention from this document, quite clearly.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: If we could now turn to 65 ter 3806, which is Y000-3262 on your index. And if you could please indicate what this document is and focus on item 1 under the order, and pay specific and particular attention to the names of the brigades.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here we have an order by Colonel Dragan Marcetic for the formation of a Vogosca Tactical Group at this time, and this time composed of a subtly different set of brigades; Ilijas, Kosevo, Vogosca, and Rajlovac brigades, and under a different commander. This time Dragan Josipovic is the commander. So here we have the formation of a tactical group that -- because it contains elements of that what was previously in the operational group, one might assume that the previous operational group had been disbanded and this is new tactical group that's been formed with some of the previous brigades and now some additional brigades. So we can see that is the type of organisation that comes together, comes apart, and is put back together in different ways entirely dependent on the situation, and in this case with a different commander.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: I would like to tender those last two documents, 65 ter 12048 and 3806.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 12048 becomes Exhibit P478, Your Honours. And document 3806 becomes Exhibit P479, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P478 and P479 are admitted into evidence. Ms. Harbour.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: And just very quickly, if we could look at 65 ter 28534. This was tendered in --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is that your last document?

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: This is my last document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: This relates to the same issue. It was tendered in the Galic case as Defence Exhibit D142.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: And, in fact, when you were being asked today by the Defence about certain responses that you gave in the Galic case, those responses were having looked at this document. That's just to orient you. You were asked today at temporary page 5 -- or, rather, at temporary page 5, Mr. Lukic quoted to you something that you said in the Galic case where you were asked: "If from this report we could conclude that the Ilijas and Igman Brigade were not part of the Vogosca Tactical Group? Here a reference to the Ilijas and Igman Brigade that you mentioned with regard to the first document I showed you today." And your answer was: "Yes, that would be a conclusion from this document on that date." Is there anything that you would like to add to the conversation you had with Mr. Lukic this morning?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Looking at paragraph 2, it appears to list various units and they appear to be a list and therefore are exclusive, by which I mean it mentions TG Vogosca and then Ilidza and then the Igman Brigade which implies from that that they are three separate organisations and that the Igman Brigade and the Ilidza Brigade on a particular date are not part of the Tactical Group Vogosca that has been formed, which links into the previous document that we've seen as well. And really this is -- this is Major-General Galic informing the Main Staff of what's occurred.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: I have no further questions for this witness, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You do not want to tender it, Ms. Harbour? This document. I mean, it's only a partial translation so --

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: Yes. Your Honour, in fact, since we received this or since it was tendered by the Galic Defence and I'm unable to determine anything about its authenticity, I wanted to show it to the witness for clarification but don't desire to tender it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. One second.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Just to resolve a very practical way, I would just like to read the relevant portion of this document into the record, that those who are studying the transcript later better understand. It is a document dated the 7th of July, 1993, coming from the SRK command and addressed to the Main Staff of the VRS, title: "Regular Combat Report With the Situation at 1700 hours." Item 2, relevant in this respect reads: "All the units are in full combat preparation and TG 'Vogosca,'" Vogosca between quotation marks, "Ilidza,s and Igm," abbreviation apparently for Igman, "Brigades are in preparation for conceivable interventions [sic] on direction of the enemy's attack." It is -- the author is mentioned, although there seems to be no signature, Major-General Stanislav Galic, and there is a stamp on the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. There is a signature, and it says "signed for him, Milosevic," with a round seal. The Chamber has no further questions. Mr. Lukic, any questions triggered by the re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We don't have anything further for this witness, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Philipps, this concludes your testimony in this Court. I would like to thank you very much for coming and for having answered all the questions that were put to you by both the parties and the Bench. I wish you a safe return home again. You may follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is the Prosecution ready to call its next witness after the break?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we take a break, and we'll resume at 27 minutes to 2.00 and we'll continue only until 2.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is the Prosecution ready to call its next witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. And if could take this opportunity to introduce to the Chamber a new member that has joined the team, it's Mr. Milbert Shin and he will be taking this next witness, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Shin. Yes. Could the witness be escorted into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Your Honours -- good afternoon, Your Honours. Good afternoon, counsel. As the witness is being led in, the Prosecution notes that in light of the Trial Chamber's rulings on adjudicated facts, it will not lead evidence that has been covered by adjudicated facts 858, 871 -- I'm sorry, 861 through 871, 893 through 895, and 1007 through 1026.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Shin. Good afternoon, Mr. Sivac.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before you give evidence the Rules require that you make a solemn declaration. May I invite you to make that solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Sivac. Please be seated. Mr. Sivac, you will first be examined by Mr. Shin. Mr. Shin is counsel for the Prosecution. You may proceed, Mr. Shin.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Sivac.

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Could you please state your full name for the record.

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: Nusret Sivac, born on the 19th of August, 1947.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: What is your current occupation?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: Currently, I work as a freelance journalist and writer.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Sivac, you have testified here at the Tribunal previously in five cases, including the Milomir Stakic case; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: And your evidence in that case was on the 29th, 30th, and 31st of July, 2002, and also on the 1st of August, 2002, and the 13th of July, 2003; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Among your prior testimony, you also testified in the Mico Stanisic and Stojan Zupljanin case on the 16th and 17th of August, 2010; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Mr. Sivac, in preparing to give evidence here today, did you have a chance to review an audio-recording of your testimony in the Stakic case?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: And did you also have an opportunity to review certain portions of your transcript in the Stanisic/Zupljanin case through the assistance of an interpreter?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Having had an opportunity to review that prior testimony, are there any corrections or clarifications that you wish to make? And just yes or no at this point, please.

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, the Prosecution will be going through these issues with the witness. In connection with this, we have provided an English version of the proofing note with these corrections or clarifications on Tuesday evening to the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Mr. Sivac, did one of those corrections or clarifications relate to a delegation visit to Omarska camp in July 1992?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: In your testimony from the Stakic case, you described the visit of Bosnian Serb officials to Omarska camp while you were a detainee there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, if I may, if the Court Officer could please put up the 65 ter 28478 and have page 51 of the e-court placed on the screen, please, for your reference.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Which is what page in the transcript?

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: In the transcript that would be T-6640.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: And I will prepared to provide the transcript page number or the e-court number, as is more convenient, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you would also provide the transcript page.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Mr. Sivac, in that testimony, you mention the following people in the delegation, and I will read them -- I will read them out.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: And Your Honours I will be beginning at line 10.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: These names are: Simo Drljaca, Milorad Vokic, Radislav Brdjanin, Mico Kovacevic, Milomir Stakic, Srdjo Srdic, Simo Miskovic, Milan Andzic, and Radmilo Zeljaja. In addition to those names just listed, were there any others that you recognised in that delegation?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: Well, no. I just recognised my journalists who were reporting on the occasion of this visit.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: If -- if I could just ask, Mr. Sivac, were there any other members of the delegation who are not named, whom I did not name in that question, that you recall at this point having seen?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: You mean the political leadership from Banja Luka? Who came there?

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Yes. That -- that is the delegation that I am referring to.

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... delegation of politicians who came from Banja Luka, this delegation was headed by Radoslav Brdjanin; there was also Radoslav Lukic [as interpreted], president of the SDS for Banja Luka; then Predrag Radic, the Mayor of Banja Luka; and Stojan Zupljanin, the chief of the centre of security services in Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Sivac. And I note that the transcript shows the name Radoslav Lukic as the president of the SDS for Banja Luka. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: No. Radoslav Vukic. It's spelled with a V.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Mr. Sivac, in addition to that delegation visit, did you wish to make corrections or clarifications relating to the organisation of Omarska camp?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: Yes, very briefly. Whenever I gave statements, I was asked about the internal organisation of the Omarska camp. As for the in-depth security of Omarska camp, it consisted of members of the Army of Republika Srpska. Now were they from the 5th Kozarske Brigade or the 43rd Brigade, they were peasants who were mobilised from the area around Omarska and they comprised the external security of Omarska camp in two circles, and there was a minefield between the two circles.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: And were there any other individuals that you recognised that you believed to be part of the army in the camp?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: Well, the internal security had a mixed composition. Members of the active-duty police, the reserve police, and mobilised soldiers of the Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Shin, could you then give us the transcript page references so that we can follow the ...

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Yes. Your Honours, this -- this clarification would relate to several points within the -- within the transcript the.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you give the range that's okay as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Okay. I may need to point to certain specific areas.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you intended to do that anyhow, then I'll not interrupt you any further.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: That's okay. Maybe this would be a good opportunity to do that. If you would just bear with me for one minute, please. I would refer Your Honours to page 6634, page 6627, page -- in a related vein, page 6639 through 6644. And that relates to the delegation visit as well. Those aspects that I have referred Your Honours to relate to elements of the security, but as the witness has explained these are clarifications to those issues. May I continue?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Mr. Sivac, in addition to the changes and clarifications you have explained to the organisation of Omarska camp, did you also wish to make corrections or additions relating to the provision of security at Trnopolje camp?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: Well, when I testified before, I said that the Trnopolje camp was secured only by soldiers of Republika Srpska. Among the guards, I recognised only two former policemen. The commander of the camp was Major Slobodan Kuruzovic and his assistants were military policemen, the Balaban brothers. The guards who guarded the camp of Trnopolje were acquaintances of mine from Prijedor, and they had been mobilised into the so-called city battalion of the Army of Republika Srpska. At guard post number 1, there was a guard who was a colleague of mine, Boro Grubic, a journalist, who sat in the same office with me ten years before that. We reported together. I reported for TV Sarajevo and he reported for the "Oslobodjenje Daily." Together with him at guard post 1 there was another acquaintance of mine, Zoran Knjeginjic. Around the camp of Trnopolje there were also the following guards: Aco Ostojic, his son Roman, his son Igor, and they all belonged to this city battalion of the Army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: And in this instance, Your Honours, I would refer you to transcript page 6753. And I note that I should have referred to that page as well in regard to the previous clarification, regarding the organisation of Omarska camp. Mr. Sivac, in addition to those clarifications, in the course of reviewing your testimony in the Stanisic/Zupljanin case, did you also notice that a certain brigade of VVRS [sic] was sometimes incorrectly noted in the English transcript, as translated to you, incorrectly noted as the 34th Motorised Brigade or the 34th Brigade in the English?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: Yes, I noticed that. Whenever I gave statements I spoke about the 43rd Motorised Brigade, and a mistake was made in the transcript. The transcript said the 34th Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, I would refer you to two instances in the proffered transcripts. Closer towards the end, transcript pages 13257 and 13258.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Mr. Sivac, apart from the corrections and clarifications you have provided here today, if you were asked the same questions about this material, would you provide the same information, in substance?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: Yes, I would.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Now that you have taken the solemn declaration, do you affirm that you provided that information in accordance with the truth?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Your Honours, the Prosecution tenders 65 ter 28478, pursuant to Rule 92 ter, as a public exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I don't know yet who to look at. Mr. Lukic? Yes. Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 28478 becomes Exhibit P480, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P480 is admitted. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would also now tender the associated exhibits to the proffered transcript, which is now P480, and I will take them in turn. 65 ter 07103.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document will receive number P481, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P481 is admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR

utterances.text: 65 ter --

utterances.text: If you would allow me to admit it first.

utterances.text: Admitted. Please proceed.

utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.text: Will receive number P484, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Your Honours, this the brief summary of Mr. Sivac's written evidence -- I'm sorry, his testimony evidence. Mr. Sivac is a Bosnian Muslim who until 1989 worked for the security service in Prijedor and in 1992 was working as a television cameraman in the same area. He provides an overview of the armed Serb take-over of Prijedor in April 1992 and the Serb attack on the area and consequent ethnic cleansing. He describes the persecution of non-Serbs and the destruction of non-Serb religious buildings and property. He was arrested by Serb police on the 10th of June, 1992, and taken to Keraterm and Omarska camps but released the same day. He was arrested again on 20 June 1992 and sent to Omarska. He describes the brutal and inhumane conditions for large numbers of non-Serbs imprisoned there, including himself. The prisoners were beaten, tortured, and killed, and women were brutally abused. In July 1992, Mr. Sivac saw a delegation of Bosnian Serb officials he recognised visit the camp, among them, Radoslav Brdjanin, Milomir Stakic, and Radmilo Zeljaja. He was transferred to Trnopolje camp on 7 August 1992, where he remained until the end of August. Your Honours, this concludes the summary of Mr. Sivac's testimony.
